no_packet.title: No packet from the node
no_packet.description: Nothing arrived from {host} on UDP port {port}. Check that 'ext UDP' is enabled on the node and that 'ext. UDP IP' points to Home Assistant, then click 'Send Position' on the node's web page and submit to try again.

web.title: Web password
web.description: If the node has a web password (--webpwd), enter it here. Home Assistant reads and switches node settings with it. Leave empty if the node has none (not recommended: without it, every device on your network can read the node's WLAN password).

reauth_confirm.title: Web password of {node}
reauth_confirm.description: The node rejected the stored web password. Enter the current one.

reconfigure.title: Web password of {node}
reconfigure.description: Enter the node's web password, or leave empty if the node has none.

udp.title: Add a MeshCom node
udp.description: Enter the IP address of your node. On the node, set 'ext. UDP IP' to the address of Home Assistant and enable 'ext UDP'. Only enable the external UDP interface on nodes that stay in your home network.

data_description.host: Private IPv4 address of the node, for example 192.168.1.50.
data_description.listen_port: The node always sends to port 1799. Only change this if a forwarder sends to another port.

user.title: Add a MeshCom node
user.description: How should Home Assistant reach the node?

menu_options.udp: External UDP (node in the home network)
menu_options.kiss: KISS over TCP (e.g. a mobile node)

kiss.title: MeshCom node via KISS
kiss.description: On the node, enable KISS (--kiss on) and, to send from Home Assistant, KISS TX (--kiss tx on). Protect the interface with authentication (--kiss auth on) and the node password (--passwd, up to 14 characters): without it, every device in the network can connect and transmit under your callsign. The node serves only one KISS client at a time; Home Assistant keeps the connection open.

data_description.callsign: The node's own callsign with SSID, e.g. QX1YZ-9. Only messages from this callsign count as sent by the node.
data_description.kiss_password: Leave empty only if KISS authentication is off on the node.

progress.wait_for_node: Waiting for a packet from the node at {host} (UDP port {port}). Click 'Send Position' on the node's web page to send one right away.

error.invalid_host: Enter a private IPv4 address, for example 192.168.1.50.
error.throttled: The node blocks logins for a minute after five failed attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
error.cannot_connect: The node's web interface cannot be reached.
error.downgrade: The node offered the secure login before and now only the unencrypted one of firmware 4.40a. Check the node's firmware and address.
error.invalid_kiss_password: The node password has 1 to 14 ASCII characters.
error.kiss_auth_required: The node asks for its password (--passwd).
error.kiss_cannot_connect: The KISS interface cannot be reached. Check --kiss on, the address and that no other KISS client is connected.

abort.port_unavailable: UDP port {port} could not be opened. Another program may be using it.

port_unavailable.message: UDP port {port} could not be opened. Another program may be using it.

sending_disabled.message: Sending is switched off for this node.

rate_limited.message: Too many messages. Wait {seconds} seconds and try again.

send_failed.message: The message could not be handed to the node.

entry_not_found.message: No MeshCom node with this ID.

entry_not_loaded.message: The MeshCom node is not loaded.

no_recipient.message: Select a group or station first.

web_auth_failed.message: The node rejected the web login.

web_throttled.message: The node blocks logins for a minute after failed attempts.

web_unavailable.message: The node's web interface cannot be reached.

web_downgrade.message: The node no longer offers the secure web login.

kiss_offline.message: The KISS connection to the node is down.

kiss_tx_off.message: The node does not allow sending via KISS (--kiss tx off).

kiss_bad_call.message: The node rejected the sender callsign.

rate_limited_node.message: The node limits sending; try again in a moment.

send_message.name: Send message
send_message.description: Sends a text message over the MeshCom network under the node's callsign. Administrators and users released in the options may send.

destination.name: Destination
destination.description: * for all, a group number or a callsign.

message.name: Message
message.description: Up to 150 bytes; umlauts count twice.

init.title: MeshCom options
init.description: Administrators may always send. Everything sent goes out on amateur radio under the node's callsign: only release users who hold a licence.

data_description.groups: Comma separated group numbers for the group select, e.g. 262, 26298.
data_description.station_mode: How heard stations appear: not at all, as a list in the attribute of the "Stations heard" sensor, or as one device per station.
data_description.station_max: Only in the mode "One device per station". Further stations are listed but get no device.
data_description.station_stale_days: A station device is removed when the station was not heard for this many days. It comes back when the station is heard again.
data_description.hide_foreign_groups: Hide messages to groups the node does not listen to (not in its group list and not configured above). Events and sensors are not affected.

error.invalid_groups: Enter up to 20 group numbers with 1 to 5 digits, separated by commas.

web_password_missing.title: MeshCom node {node} has no web password
web_password_missing.description: Without a web password, every device and every website opened in a browser on your network can read the node's WLAN password and change its settings. Set one on the node with `--webpwd` followed by the password (up to 19 characters) and enter it in Home Assistant via the integration's Reconfigure option.

web_legacy_login.title: MeshCom node {node} uses the unencrypted web login
web_legacy_login.description: Firmware 4.40a only knows a login that sends the web password unencrypted in the address, after which the node trusts Home Assistant's IP address. Home Assistant therefore logs out right after each query (every 5 minutes), so the node trusts it only for seconds. Anyone who can read your network traffic can still see the password. Update the node to a firmware with the secure login; Home Assistant then switches to it by itself and never back.

web_downgrade.title: MeshCom node {node} no longer offers the secure web login
web_downgrade.description: The node used the secure web login before and now only offers the unencrypted login of firmware 4.40a. That happens after a firmware downgrade, or if another device answers at the node's address. Home Assistant does not send the password unencrypted. Check the node; after a deliberate downgrade, remove and add the node again.

kiss_auth_off.title: KISS interface of {node} without authentication
kiss_auth_off.description: The node did not ask for a password when Home Assistant connected to its KISS interface. Every device in the network can then connect instead and, with KISS TX on, transmit under your callsign. Set a node password (--passwd) and enable KISS authentication (--kiss auth on), then enter the password in Home Assistant via the integration's Reconfigure option.
